data.name: Kamalavti
data.gender_notes: Kamalavti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Kamala (lotus) and Vati (goddess). Kamalavti is the goddess of lotus, symbolizing beauty and spiritual growth. The name Kamalavti carries the meaning “Lotus Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kamalavti usually hope their child will grow to embody lotus goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of divine beauty and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Kamalavti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lotus Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kamalavti total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In ancient Indian mythology, Kamalavati is the name of a celestial nymph, or apsara, who embodies grace and elegance, as well as the goddess of love and fertility.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the lotus symbolizes detachment, purity, and the ability to rise above difficulties and challenges. Hence, Kamalavati represents the embodiment of spiritual growth and the attainment of inner peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kamalavati, meaning 'Lotus-born', signifies the divine emergence of the soul from the lotus feet of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing spiritual growth and purity. In Hindu mythology, the lotus symbolizes enlightenment and detachment, reflecting Kamalavati's connection to the divine and her spiritual journey.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads.

historical_references.reference: Kamalavati was the queen consort of King Bhartṛhari of the Gupta Empire in the 5th century CE. She is famous for her beauty and her patronage of art and literature.

Kamalavati is also mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata. She was the wife of the sage Veda Vyasa and is revered as the goddess of learning. She is believed to have dictated the Mahabharata to her husband.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Kamalavati is derived from Sanskrit and means 'Lotus-born'. In Hindu mythology, Kamalavati is associated with the god Vishnu and is considered the embodiment of his divine consort Lakshmi, symbolizing prosperity, fertility, and good fortune. In modern contexts, this name is often seen on various social media platforms such as Reddit, Instagram, and Pinterest, reflecting contemporary trends. On Reddit, users may discuss Hindu mythology, spirituality, and feminist interpretations of Kamalavati, acknowledging her role as a powerful goddess and an inspiration for women. On Instagram, users may post images of lotus flowers, Hindu temple art, and contemporary artwork inspired by Kamalavati and her association with Lakshmi. On Pinterest, users may create boards dedicated to Hindu mythology, spiritual practices, and Kamalavati-inspired home decor, reflecting a growing interest in the intersection of spirituality and interior design. Overall, Kamalavati's modern context reflects a growing appreciation for Hindu mythology and spirituality, as well as a recognition of the importance of women and feminist interpretations in these traditions.
